question: Can ITC be claimed on input services used for exempt supplies under GST?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 16
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 16 of the CGST Act provides conditions for claiming input tax credit. ITC can be claimed only on inputs used for taxable supplies or exports, not for exempt supplies.

retrieved_documents.title: Rule 36
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Rule 36 of the CGST Rules specifies that input tax credit shall be claimed in the return for the period during which the taxpayer becomes eligible to claim such credit.

expected_answer: No, ITC cannot be claimed on input services used for exempt supplies. Section 16 of the CGST Act restricts ITC to inputs used for taxable supplies or exports only.

question: What are the conditions for claiming ITC on capital goods under GST?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 16
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: For capital goods, ITC can be claimed in installments over 60 months, with 5% of the input tax credit being blocked for each year of the remaining installment period.

retrieved_documents.title: GST Circular
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Capital goods qualify for ITC when they are used or intended to be used in the course of business for making taxable supplies.

expected_answer: ITC on capital goods can be claimed in 60 monthly installments. 5% of the input tax credit is blocked for each year of the remaining installment period. Capital goods must be used or intended for use in the course of business for making taxable supplies.

question: Can ITC be claimed on input services used for both taxable and exempt supplies?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 17
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 17(1) allows ITC on inputs used for both taxable and exempt supplies in proportion to the taxable supplies made.

retrieved_documents.title: Rule 36A
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Rule 36A provides for apportionment of input tax credit when inputs are used for both taxable and exempt supplies.

expected_answer: Yes, ITC can be claimed on input services used for both taxable and exempt supplies, but only in proportion to the taxable supplies made. The credit must be apportioned based on the ratio of taxable supplies to total supplies.

question: What is the time limit for claiming ITC on inputs under GST?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 16

question: Can ITC be claimed on input services used for non-business purposes?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 17
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 17(2) denies ITC on inputs used for non-business purposes. ITC is allowed only on inputs used or intended to be used in the course of business.

retrieved_documents.title: GST Manual
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: The GST Manual clarifies that inputs used for personal purposes or non-business activities do not qualify for ITC.

expected_answer: No, ITC cannot be claimed on input services used for non-business purposes. Section 17(2) of the CGST Act restricts ITC to inputs used or intended to be used in the course of business only.

question: What are the conditions for claiming ITC on input services used for exports?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 16
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 16(1) allows ITC on inputs used for making zero-rated supplies, including exports. ITC on exports is available without any restriction.

retrieved_documents.title: Rule 36
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Rule 36 provides that input tax credit on inputs used for exports can be claimed in the return for the period during which the export supply is made.

expected_answer: Yes, ITC can be claimed on input services used for exports without any restriction. Section 16(1) of the CGST Act allows ITC on inputs used for making zero-rated supplies, including exports.

question: Can ITC be claimed on input services used for both taxable and export supplies?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 16
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 16(1) allows ITC on inputs used for making zero-rated supplies, including exports. When inputs are used for both taxable and export supplies, ITC is available for both portions.

retrieved_documents.title: Rule 36A
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Rule 36A provides for apportionment of input tax credit when inputs are used for multiple types of supplies including taxable, exempt, and export supplies.

expected_answer: Yes, ITC can be claimed on input services used for both taxable and export supplies. The credit is available for both portions - full credit for export portion and proportionate credit for taxable portion.

question: What is the procedure for claiming ITC on input services used for mixed supplies?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 17
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 17(1) allows ITC on inputs used for both taxable and exempt supplies in proportion to the taxable supplies made.

retrieved_documents.title: Rule 36A
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Rule 36A provides the methodology for apportioning input tax credit when inputs are used for multiple types of supplies.

expected_answer: For mixed supplies, ITC must be apportioned based on the ratio of taxable supplies to total supplies. Rule 36A provides the specific methodology for calculating the apportioned credit.

question: Can ITC be claimed on input services used for development of real estate projects?

retrieved_documents.title: GST Circular
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: The GST Circular clarifies that ITC on input services used for development of real estate projects is allowed only when the project is intended for sale.

retrieved_documents.title: GST Manual
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: The GST Manual states that ITC on input services used for construction of immovable property is allowed only when the property is intended for sale.

expected_answer: ITC on input services used for development of real estate projects is allowed only when the project is intended for sale. If the property is intended for self-use or rent, ITC is not available.

question: What are the conditions for claiming ITC on input services used for making taxable supplies?

retrieved_documents.title: CGST Act, Section 16
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Section 16(1) allows ITC on inputs used for making taxable supplies. The conditions include that inputs must be used or intended to be used in the course of business.

retrieved_documents.title: Rule 36
retrieved_documents.relevant_text: Rule 36 requires that input tax credit shall be claimed in the return for the period during which the taxpayer becomes eligible to claim such credit.

expected_answer: ITC can be claimed on input services used for making taxable supplies when inputs are used or intended to be used in the course of business. The credit must be claimed in the return for the period during which the taxpayer becomes eligible to claim such credit.
